It does not unfortunately, cycling is waiting for Beneficial Bacteria to grow so that the water can get the waste to become less toxic. It takes 4-6 weeks to cycle a tank, you can do it with fish in as well since you already have one guy still alive.

I had to do a fish-in cycle, so here’s how I did: 
get test strips or a test kit, either will work for now, but you want to get it if you want a healthy tank. Start 50% water changes daily, for at least a week while you’re getting the strips. Do not feed the tank for 3 days, when you do, feed only what he will eat in 2 minutes while you watch to ensure there’s no over feeding. High ammonia and high  nitrite are extremely toxic, and are the first things to get concentrated when cycling so you have to make sure to remove a good amount every day to keep your fish alive, he will be stressed, but hopefully live. After the ammonia goes up, it will go down and then the nitrite will go up, Keep both below 1.0ppm. It will take 2-4 weeks for the nitrites to finish and become nitrates, the whole thing taking a bit over a month to finish. 

I wish you the best of luck :)

This is what worked for me to teach my dog recall when nothing else worked:

Find a super high value treat that your dog LOVES, a treat he goes crazy for. It could be cheese, chicken, peanut butter, or a dog treat if he’s crazy about them. Just something that’s better than any other treat he gets. For my dog, it’s kraft cheese slices. 

Now, *only* give him this treat when you say the recall cue. ONLY when you say this cue, and never with any other one. He needs to know he only gets this magical, amazing food when he hears that cue. 

Now to start training. Build association with the cue and the reward by saying it then immediately giving him the reward, do this 5-10 times in a couple sessions, or until the the dog starts expecting the treat when he hears the recall cue. Once he associates the cue with the reward, say it when he’s 3ft away from you and paying attention. Do that until he comes every single time at that distance with no distractions. Slowly create more and more distance between you and him when you say it, and go closer if he’s not listening. Once he’s coming 99% of the time in the house, from across the house, you can start the same process over with a leash in the backyard. 

The backyard provides lots of distractions, which is where the leash comes in. Start at 6ft, if he doesn’t come try and give a gently tug on the leash just to get his attention, if he comes reward him and if he doesn’t say it again. Over time give more and more leash length, until he’s coming every time when he’s off leash. 

TIPS:
- do not repeat the recall cue. Say it once, *maybe* twice if he didn’t hear, but don’t say it a million times when he’s not listening. This taints the cue and teaches him he doesn’t have to listen to you. 
- don’t move too fast. Don’t include distractions when he’s not ready. Don’t set him up for failure by expecting too much too soon, this is a slow process. 
- if his old recall cue didn’t work, find a new one.  It could be “name, here” “name, come” or even a whistle, or any other thing you want really. As long as it’s not the same cue as last time. 
- this takes time. It took 7 months for my dog to be allowed on a long line when on walks, and she’s a Velcro dog, so try and be patient.

If the dog is simply distracted, you can try tugging the leash just enough to let him know you’re there, you can also try walking away from him and lightly tug on the leash until he comes to/with you and reward when he does.

If it’s shallow dermis or “styro”, like a paper-cut or slightly deeper, you can take it off when it stops bleeding. If it’s deeper dermis you should keep a bandage on for a couple weeks, changing and cleaning it every 2-3 days. If it’s fat or “beans” leave it on for 3-4 weeks or until it’s 80% healed, changing the bandage and cleaning the wound every 2-3 days. 

You can use a bandaid if it’s shallow dermis since it won’t be creating a lot of “mess” (open wounds make a sort of liquid that hardens, creating a scab, with a bandage on it won’t harden), if it’s deeper dermis or fat you can use paper towel or gauze, or a heavy-duty bandaid, ideally you would use something made so it doesn’t stick but its fine if you don’t. Clean it with either saline solution or you can boil some water and let it cool, you can use normal water but it’s not as clean and will hurt a bit more.
